A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LieRE. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching of retained, revised, added, and removed content.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments on CIFAR-100, ImageNet, UCF101, and RSNA hemorrhage detection, alongside data-efficiency, generator-scaling, and patch-shuffling analyses.

after.justification: v2 reports original classification results on CIFAR-100, ImageNet-1k, and UCF101, plus scaling, parameter-sharing, efficiency, and patch-shuffling experiments, including appendix results.

M1.justification: The learned skew-symmetric generators, matrix exponentials, and key/query rotations are retained. LieRE-Commute names the 2×2 block restriction already evaluated in v1. v2 clarifies parameter sharing and evaluates sharing alternatives without changing the main LieRE procedure.

E1.justification: v2 removes the RSNA binary hemorrhage-detection experiment, eliminating the medical-imaging domain evaluated in v1. CIFAR-100, ImageNet, and UCF101 remain. The ImageNet-1k terminology does not establish different dataset coverage.

E2.justification: VisionLlama gains evaluated entries for ImageNet and UCF101, including UCF101 patch shuffling. v2 also compares LieRE-Commute separately against RoPE-Mixed across its tables and plots, distinguishing configurations that v1 conflated when identifying its 2×2 generator restriction with RoPE-Mixed.

E3.justification: v2 adds ViT-Tiny and ViT-Large evaluations around the retained ViT-B setup, parameter-sharing controls, and inference-FLOP measurements. The stated video patch size changes from 4×16×16 in v1 Appendix A.2 to 2×16×16 in v2 Appendix B.2, preventing a clean same-setting comparison of video scores.

E4.justification: v2 adds backbone-size sensitivity experiments, head/layer parameter-sharing ablations, and FLOP analyses in Sections 5.3–5.5 and Appendix B.3. These investigate capacity, sharing, and computational overhead beyond v1's generator-size, data-efficiency, and shuffling analyses. Appendix B also briefly reports a pooling comparison.

E5.justification: v1 reports point estimates without uncertainty intervals. v2 adds 95% confidence intervals to Table 1, explicitly bootstrapped intervals to Appendix Table 5, and error bars to scaling plots. Neither version specifies training-run or seed counts; the new intervals do not establish additional independent training runs.

E6.justification: Reported LieRE accuracies change from 69.4 to 69.9 on CIFAR-100, 68.8 to 69.5 on ImageNet, and 51.1 to 53.6 on UCF101. The video results accompany a changed patch size. v2 also revises baseline and shuffling results, adds scaling/sharing/FLOP results, and removes all RSNA scores.

T1.justification: Equation (2) introduces an algebraic error. After matching notation, v1's final term exp(V)^(-1) exp(U) becomes exp(U)^(-1) exp(V) in v2, while the left side remains exp(U−V). This identity is generally false even for commuting generators. The remaining mathematical development is largely retained.

C1.justification: The core encoding and efficiency contributions remain. The abstract replaces 'up to 6%' with explicitly relative improvements of up to 9.7% for 2D and 25.5% for 3D. Demonstrated applicability narrows to images and videos, and the conclusion substitutes UCF101 for medical validation; the 3.5× training and 30% data-saving claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 attributes improved RoPE-Mixed performance to parameter sharing and explains small FLOP overhead through attention dominating encoding costs. The architecture and SE(3) limitations remain substantively unchanged. The new interpretation that full sharing is best for both methods overstates Table 2, where layer-specific RoPE-Mixed performs better.

D1.justification: v2 adds concrete project/backbone links, generator implementation code in Appendix B.4, and disclosures of CLS pooling, PyTorch Lightning, and the VideoMAE dataloader. Most hardware and hyperparameters remain. Explicit subset-selection and Mixup documentation disappears; the PDFs do not establish that Mixup use actually stopped.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to positional interpolation, Focused Transformer, and PyTorch Lightning, removes the Mixup reference, and refines its relationship to RoPE-Mixed through parameter-sharing distinctions. The overall literature-review framework and principal related methods remain.

P1.justification: Substantial prose revisions affect the introduction, positional-encoding review, and experimental narrative. Section 5.3 is reorganized around three scaling axes, limitations become continuous prose, the lengthy broader-impacts discussion is condensed to one paragraph, and funding and acknowledgments are removed.

P2.justification: v2 replaces Figure 1 with an input-to-attention schematic and adds a generator/sharing comparison diagram. Separate accuracy and shuffling tables are consolidated, new ablation/FLOP/model-size tables appear, plots are redrawn and regrouped with error bars, and the algorithms change from stacked to side-by-side presentation.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, the added uncertainty reporting, scaling and FLOP analyses, clearer comparator distinctions, and implementation details improve empirical scrutiny and reproducibility. The net gain is limited by removed medical validation and new errors: Equation (2) is incorrect, and Table 2 reports 68.3 for layer-specific versus 66.9 for fully shared RoPE-Mixed despite claiming full sharing is best.
